PROJECT NO. 58482                                                   §


                                                                             BEFORE THE
RULEMAKING TO DEVELOP A RELIABILITY                                 §       PUBLIC UTILITY
SERVICE TO COMPETITIVELY PROCURE DEMAND                             §        COMMISSION
                                                                              OF TEXAS
REDUCTIONS FROM LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS                                §

UNDER PURA § 39.170(b)                                              §



                   COMMENTS OF MODERN TEX CONSULTING LLC

 ON PERFORMANCE REPORTING AND EVALUATION UNDER PROPOSED 16 TAC
                            § 25.521
 TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:

 Modern Tex Consulting LLC ("Modern Tex") submits these comments regarding proposed 16

 Texas Administrative Code § 25.521 establishing the Large Load Demand Management Service

 ("LLDMS"). The proposed rule would implement PURA § 39.170 by requiring ERCOT to

 develop a reliability service that competitively procures demand reductions from qualifying large

 load customers and by establishing the operational framework governing the service.1

 The principal policy decision in this proceeding has already been made. The Legislature

 determined that ERCOT should possess a tool to procure demand reductions from large load

 customers. The proposed rule appropriately implements that directive. Modern Tex does not ask

 the Commission to prescribe procurement quantities, deployment triggers, compensation levels,




 1 Project No. 58482, Large Load Demand Management Service, Proposal for Publication of
 New 16 TAC § 25.521 at 1, 6-7 (July 24, 2026) (PFP); Public Utility Regulatory Act, Tex. Util.
 Code Ann. § 39.170 (West Supp. 2026) (PURA).


                 Comments of Modern Tex Consulting LLC in Project No. 58482 - Page 1
 customer eligibility, or operational criteria. Those judgments are appropriately entrusted to

ERCOT.2

Modern Tex's concern is narrower.

The proposed rule grants ERCOT substantial discretion regarding procurement, deployment, and

administration of LLDMS. That flexibility is both reasonable and necessary. Reliability

conditions change, and ERCOT must be able to respond to those changes. But if the Commission

grants discretion, it should also retain the ability to evaluate how that discretion is exercised.

Importantly, the Commission has already recognized this principle. Proposed § 25.521(h) would

require ERCOT to provide after-action reporting following procurement events. Modern Tex

supports that approach. The question presented here is whether the reporting requirement

provides sufficient information to permit meaningful evaluation of the program over time.3

These comments do not address procurement quantity, bidding methodology, deployment

authority, customer eligibility, compensation levels, or the appropriate annual program budget.

They address only the Commission's ability to evaluate the effectiveness of the program after

implementation.


                             I. INTEREST OF THE COMMENTER
Modern Tex is a Texas-based policy advisory and consulting firm concerned with the lawful,

administrable, transparent, and cost-effective implementation of Texas energy policy in the

ERCOT region.

Modern Tex submits these comments on its own behalf. These comments were not

commissioned or funded by any client, and Modern Tex does not represent a large load



2 PFP at 7-12.
3 PFP at 12-13.


                  Comments of Modern Tex Consulting LLC in Project No. 58482 - Page 2
 customer, electric utility, qualified scheduling entity, retail electric provider, or other market

participant in this proceeding.

That position allows Modern Tex to occupy a limited but useful role in this record. Modern Tex

does not benefit from maximizing or minimizing LLDMS procurement, selecting one

deployment threshold over another, or influencing compensation levels paid to participating

customers. Its interest is ensuring that the Commission's chosen framework preserves ERCOT's

operational flexibility while also preserving the information necessary to evaluate whether the

program is achieving its intended purpose.


 II. THE COMMISSION CORRECTLY RECOGNIZED THAT REPORTING SHOULD
                     ACCOMPANY THE PROGRAM
The record reflects increasing attention to the reliability implications of rapid large-load growth

in ERCOT. The Legislature responded by enacting PURA § 39.170 and directing the

Commission to require ERCOT to develop a service capable of competitively procuring demand

reductions from large load customers during anticipated emergency conditions. The proposed

rule implements that directive.4

The question before the Commission therefore is not whether ERCOT should have this authority.

The Legislature has already answered that question.

Nor is the question whether ERCOT should possess operational flexibility. It should.

The question is whether the Commission will have sufficient information to determine whether

the program is succeeding.

Staff appropriately recognized the importance of that issue by including proposed § 25.521(h),

which would require ERCOT to file an after-action report identifying the number of offers



4 PFP at 1, 6-7.


                   Comments of Modern Tex Consulting LLC in Project No. 58482 - Page 3
 received, the quantity procured, pricing information, deployment information, and

recommendations for revision. Modern Tex supports that requirement.5

The proposed reporting provision serves an important purpose: it allows the Commission to

understand what occurred during a particular procurement event.

But the Commission may ultimately need to answer different questions. How many customers

are participating? What are the program's annual costs? How often are procured resources

available? How does the cost of LLDMS compare to alternative reliability tools? Has the

program provided measurable value over time?

Event-specific reporting and program-level evaluation serve different purposes. Both are useful.

Both can be accomplished without constraining ERCOT's operational discretion.


           III. MODEST EXPANSION OF THE REPORTING REQUIREMENT
Modern Tex does not recommend replacing proposed § 25.521(h). Rather, Modern Tex

recommends modest additions to the existing reporting requirement so that the Commission can

evaluate not only individual procurement events, but also overall program performance.

Specifically, Modern Tex recommends that proposed § 25.521(h) be supplemented to require

reporting of:

   •   total annual LLDMS expenditures;

   •   the number of participating large load customers;

   •   availability performance metrics;

   •   annual deployment frequency and duration;

   •   cost-per-megawatt and, where applicable, cost-per-megawatt-hour metrics; and

   •   comparisons to other reliability services when reasonably available.


5 PFP at 12-13.


                  Comments of Modern Tex Consulting LLC in Project No. 58482 - Page 4
 Those additions would also help answer questions the Commission expressly invited

commenters to address. The PFP asks whether the proposed $54 million annual budget is

appropriate and whether customers that are available but not deployed should receive some

percentage of the market clearing price for availability. Modern Tex takes no position in these

comments on the correct annual budget or the appropriate level of availability compensation. But

those questions are difficult to answer well without program-level information concerning

expenditures, availability performance, deployment frequency, and cost effectiveness over time.6

Modern Tex respectfully proposes the following additions to proposed § 25.521(h):

       (9) total program expenditures for the calendar year;

       (10) the number of participating large load customers by procurement period;

       (11) availability performance during each LLDMS obligation period;

       (12) annual deployment frequency and duration;

       (13) cost per megawatt procured and, where applicable, cost per megawatt-hour
       of demand reduction achieved; and

       (14) any cost-effectiveness metrics or comparisons to other reliability services
       that ERCOT determines are appropriate for evaluating program performance.
The Commission has already concluded that reporting should accompany the service. The

recommendation offered here merely expands the Commission's ability to evaluate that

information.

The proposed additions would not alter procurement authority. They would not establish

procurement targets. They would not prescribe deployment criteria. They would not require

disclosure of customer-specific commercially sensitive information. They would simply allow

the Commission to evaluate whether LLDMS is delivering reliability benefits that justify its cost.



6 PFP at 5.


                Comments of Modern Tex Consulting LLC in Project No. 58482 - Page 5
                           IV. DISCRETION REQUIRES EVALUATION
One principle governs these comments.

ERCOT should have the flexibility necessary to operate LLDMS as an effective reliability tool.

But flexibility and accountability are not competing concepts.

A regulatory framework can preserve ERCOT's operational discretion while also preserving the

Commission's ability to evaluate the results of that discretion. The choice is not between

flexibility and oversight.

The Commission has already recognized as much through proposed § 25.521(h). The remaining

question is whether the reporting requirement is sufficiently robust to permit meaningful

evaluation of program performance over time.7

Without program-level reporting, the Commission may know that demand reductions were

procured during a particular event. It may not know whether procurement was appropriately

sized, frequently deployed, unusually costly, or materially effective relative to other reliability

tools.

With modest additional reporting, the Commission can preserve ERCOT's flexibility while

maintaining the factual record necessary to evaluate whether the program is achieving its

intended purpose.


                                          V. CONCLUSION
The Legislature determined that ERCOT should possess a tool to competitively procure demand

reductions from qualifying large load customers. The proposed rule appropriately implements

that directive, and Modern Tex supports its adoption.8



7 PFP at 12-13.
8 PFP at 1, 6-7.


                   Comments of Modern Tex Consulting LLC in Project No. 58482 - Page 6
 The Commission has also recognized that the use of this tool should be accompanied by

reporting and has included an after-action reporting requirement in proposed § 25.521(h).

Modern Tex agrees with that judgment.9

Modern Tex does not ask the Commission to alter the structure of LLDMS, modify ERCOT's

procurement authority, or constrain ERCOT's operational discretion. It asks only that the

Commission modestly expand the reporting framework so that it may evaluate not only

individual procurement events, but the effectiveness of the program as a whole.

The Legislature determined that ERCOT should have this tool, and the Commission

appropriately proposes to implement that directive. Modern Tex asks only that the Commission

retain sufficient information to evaluate whether the program is accomplishing the purpose for

which it was created.


Respectfully submitted,

Raven S. Kyles
State Bar No. 24110860
Modern Tex Consulting LLC
12645 Memorial Dr., Ste. F1, PMB 643
Houston, Texas 77024-4979
346-616-1321
info@moderntexconsulting.com

COUNSEL FOR MODERN TEX CONSULTING LLC

Dated: August 18, 2026




9 PFP at 12-13.


                  Comments of Modern Tex Consulting LLC in Project No. 58482 - Page 7
                                    EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

                             MODERN TEX CONSULTING LLC

                                      PROJECT NO. 58482
Modern Tex supports adoption of proposed 16 TAC § 25.521 establishing the Large Load

Demand Management Service. Modern Tex also supports Staff's decision to require after-action

reporting under proposed § 25.521(h).

Modern Tex recommends supplementing, not replacing, that reporting framework with limited

program-level metrics so the Commission can evaluate the overall effectiveness, cost, and

reliability value of LLDMS over time.

   •   Retain proposed § 25.521(h)'s after-action reporting framework.

   •   Add annual program-level reporting for expenditures, participation, availability

       performance, and deployment frequency and duration.

   •   Include cost-per-megawatt and, where applicable, cost-per-megawatt-hour metrics,

       together with reasonable comparisons to other reliability services where available.

   •   Use program-level reporting to inform future review of the annual budget and availability

       compensation, without taking a position on those issues here.

   •   Protect participant-specific commercially sensitive information through aggregation or

       anonymization.

   •   Preserve ERCOT's procurement authority, deployment authority, and operational

       discretion while giving the Commission the record needed to evaluate program

       performance.

Modern Tex asks only that the Commission retain sufficient information to evaluate whether the

tool it is creating is accomplishing its intended purpose.
